title: Dictionary pattern A - Group rows by customer
summary: Coding / Python / Dictionaries / Grouping and state

children.text: Given a list of order dictionaries, return a dictionary from customer_id to that customer's rows. Preserve input order within each group.

items: Choose customer_id as the dictionary key.
Initialize a list for the first row of a group.
Append subsequent rows to that list.
Check empty input and interleaved customers.

children.text: The key selects the group; the dictionary value stores the growing list. Every row must be appended rather than replacing the previous list.
defaultdict(list) makes initialization implicit. Both versions assume customer_id exists and is hashable.
Expected O(n) dictionary work for n rows under ordinary hash-table assumptions. Stored row references require O(n) output space.

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: Assigning groups[key] = row on every iteration retains only the last row.

items: How would you produce total revenue instead of lists?
